recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared types & Audit foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency leaf modules. shared-types defines enums (LeaveStatus, LeaveType) and BaseEntity used by every other module. Audit module has no domain dependencies and is required by GP-002 for all state-changing operations.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Employee lookup is a prerequisite for leave-request (submitter validation, manager resolution) and leave-balance (employee existence check).

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Leave Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on shared-types. Policy definitions (entitlement, approval rules) are needed before balance initialization and request validation can reference them.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — Leave Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-types, employee, and leave-policy. Balance must exist before leave-request can deduct/validate sufficiency. Contains the core balance lifecycle: initialization, deduction, restoration.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Leave Request module (core workflow)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all prior modules. Orchestrates the full leave workflow: submit (validates employee, policy, balance sufficiency; creates request; records audit), approve/reject (manager authorization, balance deduction on approval, audit), cancel (restore balance, audit). This is the largest module.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: shared-types (src/shared/types/) is the innermost layer holding cross-module enums and BaseEntity. Domain modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit) each own their entity, repository interface, service interface, and service implementation. leave-request is the orchestration module that wires the workflow together — it depends on all other modules but none depend on it. Controllers and routes live in the same module directory as their service, following the existing uptime/status pattern. All state-changing operations in leave-request (submit, approve, reject, cancel) must call IAuditService.record per GP-002. RBAC is enforced at the route level via middleware (not inline) per GP-005 — leave-request routes will use a requireRole guard. Balance deduction on approval and restoration on cancellation are transactional: if the balance operation fails, the request status change must roll back.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — calendar days or business days (Mon–Fri excluding holidays)?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction arithmetic in LeaveBalanceService.deductBalance, sufficiency checks in hasSufficientBalance, and date-range validation in LeaveRequestService.submit. If business days, a holiday calendar dependency is needed.
candidate_options: Calendar days (simplest; every day between startDate and endDate counts)
Business days (Mon–Fri only; requires weekday computation)
Business days with holiday exclusion (requires a holiday calendar module)

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } where UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route guard applied at the Fastify route registration level — never inline in handlers. Employees can submit/cancel their own leave requests. Managers can approve/reject requests for their direct reports (verified via employee.managerId). HR admins have full access to all leave operations.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code: VALIDATION_ERROR). Authentication failure → 401 (code: UNAUTHORIZED). Authorization failure → 403 (code: FORBIDDEN). Not found → 404 (code: NOT_FOUND). Insufficient balance → 400 (code: INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE). Policy violation (e.g. minimum notice not met) → 400 (code: POLICY_VIOLATION). Inactive employee → 400 (code: EMPLOYEE_INACTIVE).
